NAME: agconv
SCENARIO NAME: Agricultural demand convergence time to function
DEFINITION: Agricultural demand convergence time to function
Parameter Explanation: Agriculture demand convergence time, represents the time required  for agricultural demand to converge to the function's predicted values, in years. Initial country data may deviate From cross-sectional predictions due to possible data errors or unique country factors. This parameter assumes that over time, such discrepancies will align with the predicted values. A high value like 10000 stops convergence; a low value like 10 speeds it up.

NAME: qem
DISPLAY NAME: Capital Costs-to-Output, Ratio in Energy, Multiplier (qem)
SCENARIO NAME: Q (capital costs-to-output ratio) in energy, multiplier
DEFINITION: Q (capital costs-to-output ratio) in energy, multiplier
Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy capital output, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the amount of capital required per unit of energy output and lower values decrease it. Lower this parameter gradually over time to simulate a decreased cost of an energy form (such as renewable energy) as a result of technological advance.  Raise it over time to simulate the addition to the capital cost of an energy form (say nuclear) as a result of the addition to those costs of environmental ones.

NAME: QE(Oil)
SCENARIO NAME: Q (capital costs-to-output ratio), currency/barrel
DEFINITION: Amount of capital required per unit of energy production (Oil)
Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QE is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on car sales by country/region and car type.  A value of 1.0 leaves car sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double car sales of the specified type relative to the base case (total car sales will be normalized and therefore unchanged relative to the base case).

SCENARIO NAME: Car sales, total multiplier
DEFINITION: Car sales, total multiplier
Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on total car sales by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves total sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double total sales relative to the base case (sales by type will not always change proportionately, because of differing relationships with total sales).

NAME: carsconv
SCENARIO NAME: Car sales, convergence time to functions
DEFINITION: Car sales, convergence time to functions
Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for car sales in years. This value determines the number of years over which all countries/regions will converge to the chosen function (as determined by the switch, vehfuncsw) for the computation of car sales per year.  A value of 10000 would effectively turn off convergence, so that initial country-specific variations From the function would be maintained over time.  A value of 60 would lead to near convergence by the middle of the 21st century.  Very rapid convergence seems improbable in the face of fundamental country differences in infrastructure, land area, culture, etc.

NAME: carabr
DISPLAY NAME: Carbon Atmospheric Absorption Non-Forest Sinks, Rate (carabr)
SCENARIO NAME: Carbon (atmospheric) absorbed yearly by oceans and non-forest land sources
DEFINITION: Carbon (atmospheric) absorbed yearly by oceans and non-forest land sources
Parameter Explanation: Rate of carbon absorption - this parameter defines the amoung of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that oceans or other sinks (except forests) absorb each year. Although this value should ultimately be a function of the carbon in the atmosphere and the carbon in the sinks of the ocean, land, and biological systems (and hence a computed variable), it is common in atmospheric models to specify it as a single, constant parameter.

SCENARIO NAME: Carbon dioxide in atmosphere, pre-industrial
DEFINITION: Carbon dioxide in atmosphere, pre-industrial

DEFINITION: Carbon generated by burning coal
DISPLAY UNITS: Billion Tons per Barrel Oil Equivalent
Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning coal expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

SCENARIO NAME: Carbon generated by burning oil
DEFINITION: Carbon generated by burning oil
DISPLAY UNITS: Billion Tons per Barrel Oil Equivalent

NAME: carforst
SCENARIO NAME: Carbon sequestered by forests
DEFINITION: Carbon sequestered by forests, gigatons per million hectaresx
Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by deforestation - this parameter specifies the amount of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that will be added by deforestation (expressed in billion hectares of land). Normally you would not change this parameter over time, because it should be a fairly fixed parameter.

NAME: carbtax
SCENARIO NAME: Carbon tax
DEFINITION: Carbon tax
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the carbon tax, expressed in dollars/ton of carbon generated and affects (increases) energy prices and (decreases) demand. Values will normally be above 50 and as an example, a value of 100 ($100/ton) will add about $0.20 to the price of a gallon of gas.

NAME: wpsysgr
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Dispute Probability with Global Economic Growth, Level (wpsysgr)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, change in dispute probability with global economic growth
DEFINITION: World politics, change in dispute probability with global economic growth
Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute probability with global economic growth. The value is in percent. Thus 0.1 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 0.1% for each percentage point increase in global economic growth relative to the long-term average.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

NAME: hltechlinc
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Health Technology for Low Incomeo Countries, Rate (hltechssa)
SCENARIO NAME: Tec Factor for Low Inc Countries
DEFINITION: Technological Factor for Other Low Income Countries

NAME: hltechssa
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Health Technology for Sub-Saharan Africa, Rate (hltechssa)
SCENARIO NAME: Tec Factor for SSA
DEFINITION: Technological Factor for South Saharan Africa

NAME: wpconsq
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Threat with Change in Power Concentration, Level (wpconsq)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, change in dispute threat with change in power concentration
DEFINITION: World politics, change in dispute threat with change in power concentration
Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with the square of change in power concentration (see also wpcon).  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on the square of global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges From approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product of the parameter and the square of concentration From year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

NAME: wpcon
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Threat with Power Concentration, Level (wpcon)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, change in dispute threat with power concentration
DEFINITION: World politics, change in dispute threat with power concentration
Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with power concentration.  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges From approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product From year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

NAME: wptrade
DISPLAY NAME: Change in Threat with Systemic Trade, Relationship (wptrade)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, change in dispute threat with systemic trade
DEFINITION: World politics, change in dispute threat with systemic trade
Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with systemic trade.  The value is in percent. Thus -0.01% would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would fall by 0.01% for every percentage increase in world trade as a percent of global GDP.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

NAME: wpindsw
SCENARIO NAME: THREAT Model Switch
DEFINITION: THREAT Model Switch: 0 indicates the base monadic model; 5 indicates the directed dyadic MIE version, 6-9 indicates undirected dyadic Rivalry versions, 10 indicates the undirected dyadic UCDP-PRIO version; Strong caution advised for all values other than 5 and 0, likely deprecated.
Parameter Explanation: A switch that can be used to turn on or off the calculations of Character of Bilateral State Interaction Score.  A value of 0 turns it off and a value greater than 0 turns it on.  1 is used to save threat, 2 is used to save Liberal Index, 3 is used to save Realist Index and 4 is used to save the COI.

SCENARIO NAME: Relationship between Child Stunting and Communicable Diseases
DEFINITION: Relationship between Child Stunting and Communicable Diseases (1=On, 0=Off)
Parameter Explanation: Switch that activates relationship between child stunting and communicable diseases. This relationship is used in the Health module to affect Communicable Diseases (Diarrhea, Respiratory Infections and Other CDs) when Child Stunting level changes From the expected value.

NAME: cdmf
SCENARIO NAME: Civilian damage that war does to economy/population
DEFINITION: Civilian damage factor in war; portion of economy
Parameter Explanation: Civilian damage factor.  This reactivity parameter links the severity of conventional war and the power of the opposing alliance to civilian damage (both population killed and economic capital destroyed).  A value of 0 will uncouple conventional war From damage and a value of 1 will make damage proportional to the war severity and opposing power.  There is no comparable parameter for the impact of nuclear war on civilians because the model always assumes civilian damage; in fact, it extends some such damage beyond the regions involved in nuclear war to third party countries (From fall-out and other collateral damage).

NAME: CIVDM
DEFINITION: Civilian damage From war;mult for pop & capital stock

DEFINITION: Climate chnge to econ impact, portion affecting  productivity or capital stocks
Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the share of production function (technology and/or climate stock) that climate change to economic impact variable eliminates. For example, CLIMECONIMP of 2 percent times 0.5 will indicate a 1 percent reduction of stock in capital/technology.

Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the use of condoms among 15-24 year olds in high risk-sex cases. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

NAME: wpterdisp
DISPLAY NAME: Conflict Arising From Territorial Disputes, Relationship (wpterdisp)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, increase in militarized dispute prob with territorial dispute
DEFINITION: World politics, increase in militarized dispute prob with territorial dispute
Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in militarized dispute probability with territorial dispute. The value is in percent. Thus 5.0 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 5.0% if they have a territorial dispute outstanding, relative to the same pair without such a dispute.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

NAME: sfintlwaralltoginidom
SCENARIO NAME: Conflict to Gini multiplier
DEFINITION: Conflict to Gini multiplier (Base equals 1)
Parameter Explanation: This parameter serves as a multiplier that adjusts the Gini coefficient based on the probability of conflict. It amplifies the Gini index by the set multiplier amount in response to the likelihood of conflict. For example, a multiplier of 1.02 typically suggests a 2% increase in the Gini coefficient. However, the actual increase is adjusted by the probability of conflict; thus, with a 50% probability of conflict, the Gini coefficient would only increase by 1%.

DEFINITION: Target growth in cultivated land
Parameter Explanation: Target annual growth rate in cultivated land, by region represents the desired annual growth rates for expanding cultivated land. NAME: CULTREG
DEFINITION: Cultural region designation, From World Values Survey

NAME: cultshmp
DISPLAY NAME: Cultural Region Shift on Materialism/Postmaterialism, Additive Factor (cultshmp)
SCENARIO NAME: Cultural region shift on materialism/postmaterialism
DEFINITION: Cultural region shift on materialism/postmaterialism
Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the materialism/post-materialism index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for materialism/post-materialism for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined From data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

NAME: democimpus
DISPLAY NAME: Democracy Impetus by Leading Power, Exogoenous Specification (democimpus)
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy impetus by the US/other leadership, 1-10 (10=most); Polity scale
DEFINITION: Democracy impetus by the US/other leadership, 1-10 (10=most); Polity scale
Parameter Explanation: Democracy impetus coming From US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  Values are on a 1-10 (10=most) scale, related to the Polity democracy scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

NAME: democimpoth
DISPLAY NAME: Democracy Impetus by Other Powers, Exgoenous Specification (democimpoth)
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy impetus From non-specific forces, 0 is neutral; Polity scale
DEFINITION: Democracy impetus From non-specific forces, 1-10 (10=most); Polity scale
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy impetus From non-specific forces such as the spread of a systemic value around democracy. The scale ranges From 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

NAME: democimpusn
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy impetus From US, neutral level, 1-10 (10=most); Polity scale
DEFINITION: Democracy impetus From US, neutral level, 1-10 (10=most); Polity scale
Parameter Explanation: The neutral or normal level of democracy impetus coming From US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  The scale ranges From 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity democracy scale.   Interventions with the parameter would be very uncommon and would normally change its value for all points in time.

NAME: eldemocimp
SCENARIO NAME: Elasticity of democracy levels with leadership
DEFINITION: Elasticity of democracy levels with leadership
Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of democracy levels with systemic leadership.  That is, the responsiveness of democracy in a country to the impetus towards democracy provided by countries/regions such as the EU or the U.S.

NAME: DEMOCWVCOUNT
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy wave counter: years current wave direction has been running
DEFINITION: Years current wave direction has been running

NAME: DEMOCWVDIR
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy wave direction at beginning of run (-1 down, 1 up)
DEFINITION: Democracy wave direction: 1 being pro-democracy, -1 being anti-democracy, 0 being no wave effect

NAME: democwvlen
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy wave length in years (peak to trough/half-wave)
DEFINITION: Democracy wave length in years (peak to trough/half-wave)
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy wave length in years (peak to trough/half-wave).  Historical waves of democracy have been variable in length, so it is very reasonable to speculate that they could change From the base value or over time.

NAME: democwvmax
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy wave, maximum amplitude in Polity scale points
DEFINITION: Democracy wave, maximum amplitude in Polity scale points
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the maximum amplitude in Polity scale points for democracy wave.  Because the Polity democracy scale runs From 1-10 (10=most democratic), it would be highly improbable that the amplitude of any wave be more than 5-6 points.

NAME: DEMOCWAVE
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy wave value in Polity scale points
DEFINITION: Democracy wave value in Polity scale points

NAME: democm
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy level multiplier
DEFINITION: Democracy multiplier
Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of democracy, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, users should not generally  change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

NAME: democconv
SCENARIO NAME: Democracy, convergence time to expected value
DEFINITION: Democracy, convergence time to expected value
Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the convergence time of political variables (DEMOC) to predicted value. Very often initial data values for countries will differ From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

NAME: dkl
DISPLAY NAME: Depreciation Rate of Agricultural Land Investment, Level (dkl)
SCENARIO NAME: Depreciation rate of agricultural land investment
DEFINITION: Depreciation coefficient for agricultural land investment
Parameter Explanation: Depreciation coefficient for agricultural land investment.  This scalar (not specific to country/region) indicates the portion (e.g., 0.01 is 1%) of the investment in agricultural land (e.g. terracing or irrigation) that depreciates in a given year.  Raising it would lead to greater requirements of agricultural investment in land to maintain that land in production.

NAME: desali
DISPLAY NAME: Desalination Responsiveness to Change in Stock, Level, Relationship (desald)
SCENARIO NAME: desalination responsiveness to change in stock levels of price
DEFINITION: desalination responsiveness to change in stock levels of price
Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in stock/inventory levels.

NAME: dstlen
DISPLAY NAME: Desired Energy Stock, Level as Portion of Stock Base, Share (dstlen)
SCENARIO NAME: Desired level of energy stocks or inventories
DEFINITION: Desired energy stock level as portion of stock base
Parameter Explanation: Desired energy stock level as portion of stock base.  It is in proportional terms so that 0.2 represents a 20% target stock level (of a base that usually includes annual production and may include demand, exports, or imports).  There is little reason for most users to want to change this parameter.

NAME: dstl
SCENARIO NAME: Desired stock (inventory) level in the economy
DEFINITION: Desired stock (inventory) level in the economy
Parameter Explanation: Desired level of stock or inventory within the economy, represented as a percentage. A value of 0.1, for instance, indicates a target stock level of 10% relative to the base case that often includes annual production and may also encompass demand, exports, or imports.

NAME: wpgreat1
DISPLAY NAME: Dyadic Dispute Probability One Great Power, Level (wpgreat1)
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with one great power
DEFINITION: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with one great power
Parameter Explanation: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with one great power.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at least one member of the dyad is a great power (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 0.7 would indicate that the existence of one great power would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.7%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at both members of the dyad are great powers (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 2.0 would indicate that the existence of two great powers would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 2.0%, all else being equal.   Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted From other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).  This addition would be on top of the increment already added for the presence of one great power in a dyad (see wpgreat1).

NAME: enconv
SCENARIO NAME: Energy demand convergence time to predicted values
DEFINITION: Energy demand convergence time to predicted values
Parameter Explanation: Energy demand convergence time to predicted values, in years.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as energy demand in this case, will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship or other relationship used in the model.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

NAME: elasdi
SCENARIO NAME: Elasticity of energy discoveries to prices
DEFINITION: Elasticity of energy discoveries to prices
Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy discoveries to prices.  This value should be positive and normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value From specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in energy markets.

NAME: rdinr
DISPLAY NAME: Energy Discovery in Basic Annual Increment, Rate (rdinr)
SCENARIO NAME: Rate of discovery of energy, basic annual increment
DEFINITION: Rate of discovery of energy, basic annual increment
Parameter Explanation: Rate of discovery of energy, basic annual increment.  This parameter determines the basic rate of additions to initial annual rates of fossil fuel discoveries.  That rate may not persist, however, because as resource bases near exhaustion, they gradually constrain discovery rates.

NAME: ENX
SCENARIO NAME: Energy exports
DEFINITION: Energy exports in billion of barrels of oil

NAME: enxm
SCENARIO NAME: Energy exports multiplier
DEFINITION: Energy exports multiplier
Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy exports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

NAME: enml
SCENARIO NAME: Energy imports limit
DEFINITION: Energy import limit
Parameter Explanation: Energy import limit, expressed in billion barrels of oil equivalent functions both as a switch and a numerical value, with 0 indicating no limit and positive values setting a specific limit. Positive values (above .001) limit imports to the value specified.  For instance, a specification for a country of 0 for the first five years, 2 for the next three, and 0 thereafter,  introduces a constrain on imports of two billion barrels per year during the sixth, seventh, and eighth years.  Restrictions of this kind are more often posed by exporters (see enxl) than importers.

NAME: ENM

DEFINITION: Energy imports in billion of barrels of oil

NAME: enmm
SCENARIO NAME: Energy imports multiplier
DEFINITION: Energy imports multiplier
Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase material input and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

DEFINITION: Government financial balances, convergence time to global functions
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of government financial balances to its global function. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in dispute probability with 10% greater power parity.  The value is in percent. NAME: malnconv
SCENARIO NAME: Malnutrition, convergence time to expected value
DEFINITION: Malnutrition, convergence time to expected value
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of political variables to its expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

NAME: mortconv
SCENARIO NAME: Mortality, convergence time to expected value
DEFINITION: Mortality, convergence time to expected value
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of mortality to its expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

NAME: sfconv
SCENARIO NAME: State failure, convergence time to expected value
DEFINITION: State failure, convergence time to expected value
Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of state failure to its expected value. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much From values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on terms of trade.  The default value of this parameter is 1.0, signifying no exogenous shift in the terms of trade between more and less economically developed countries.  Relative prices in various sectors, particularly agriculture and energy, will still change endogenously.  A value greater than 1.0 additionally improves terms of trade for LDCs at the expense of developed countries.  A value of less than 1.0 shifts terms of trade to the benefit of wealthier countries.  A value of 1.2 would improve the terms of trade of the very least developed countries by about 20 percent.  This parameter should not normally be changed From 1 in the initial year. NAME: reac
DISPLAY NAME: Threat Magnitude Felt by Target Response to Changing Power Balance, Reactivity (reac)
SCENARIO NAME: Reactivity of countries to threat From each other, military spending
DEFINITION: Reactivity of countries to threat From each other, military spending
Parameter Explanation: Reactivity (Actor, Target).  This parameter determines the magnitude of the threat felt by a target in response to changing power balances with respect to an actor.  A value of 1.5 means that the perceived threat shifts 50 percent faster than the power balance, while a value of .5 means that threat rises only 50 percent as fast.  The user should be aware, however, that in the calculation of how threat affects defense spending, reactivities to ALL actors will shape a country's/region's expenditures, thus often diffusing sensitivity to changes in power of only a single external actor.  By setting reac for all actors towards a target to 0.0, then focusing the attention of a target on a single actor (e.g. reac(Russia, China) = 1.0), you can eliminate that diffusion of attention.

NAME: wpthrconv
SCENARIO NAME: World politics, convergence time to predicted underlying threat levels
DEFINITION: World politics, convergence time to predicted underlying threat levels
Parameter Explanation: World politics, convergence time to predicted underlying threat levels.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as dyadic conflict in this case, will differ a little or much From values predicted by broader empirical analysis across states (and possibly across time).  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or idiosyncratic factors.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will very often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country- or dyad-specific "shift" should disappear.  A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.  It is possible to set this parameter to 1, thereby replacing the empirical value by predicted values already in the first year and then every year thereafter.

NAME: QEUNCON(Oil)
SCENARIO NAME: Q (capital costs-to-output ratio), unconventional, currency/barrel
DEFINITION: Capital required per unit of energy production for unconventional energy sources (Oil)
Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QEUNCON is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

NAME: QEUNCON(OthRenew)
SCENARIO NAME: Q (capital costs-to-output ratio), unconventional, currency/barrel
DEFINITION: Capital required per unit of energy production for unconventional energy sources (OthRenew)
Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QEUNCON is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

NAME: wvsagesw
DISPLAY NAME: World Value Survey Aging Function, Switch (wvsagesw)
SCENARIO NAME: World Value Survey aging function switch
DEFINITION: World Value Survey aging function switch
Parameter Explanation: Switch for World Value Survets aging.  The parameter controls the dynamics associated with the value orientation of cohorts in the model.  The standard value for it is 2, which results in the "aging" of value orientations.  That is, value orientation is calculated From GDP per capita only for the youngest cohort; all others carry their orientation forward in time.  Any other value for wvsagesw (the WVS aging switch) will result in use of the cohort-specific functions with GDP per capita.
